title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'équation des lacets' in its GL(2) shadow. Let A = Z, Z_l or Ẑ. Take rho = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (det 1, trace 1, order 6) and sigma = [[0,-1],[1,0]] (det 1, trace 0, order 4); together they generate SL2(Z). Given xi = [[A,B],[C,D]] and eta = [[R,S],[T,U]], one asks for alpha (resp. beta) in GL(2,A) with [alpha,rho] = xi (resp. [beta,sigma] = eta).

The equation is equivalent to alpha rho alpha^{-1} = xi rho. So xi rho must be GL2(A)-conjugate to rho. The necessary numerical conditions are det = 1 and the trace condition (16)/(29).

The page finishes the previous page's Proposition.

(1) Solvability needs the second condition that xi rho be regular, i.e. never scalar on any fibre. Equivalently, xi is not congruent to a scalar multiple of rho^{-1} = [[1,-1],[1,0]] modulo any maximal ideal. It suffices that D be invertible, since the (2,2) entry of rho^{-1} is 0. Likewise for eta: it suffices that U be invertible, since the (2,2) entry of sigma^{-1} = [[0,1],[-1,0]] is 0.

(2) When this holds there is always a solution with det alpha = ±1 (resp. det beta = ±1). Modern justification:
- A regular 2x2 matrix over a local ring is cyclic, hence conjugate to the companion matrix of its characteristic polynomial. Over Z one uses class number 1 of Z[zeta_6] and of Z[i].
- The solutions form a torsor under the centraliser A[rho]^x = A[zeta_6]^x (resp. A[i]^x).
- So det alpha is well defined modulo norms of units. For l ≠ 3 (resp. l ≠ 2) the extension is unramified and the norm is onto Z_l^x.
- For l = 3 (resp. l = 2) the cokernel is {±1}. For example, -1 is not a norm from Q_3(sqrt -3).

(3) Hence a solution exists in SL(2,A) iff the residual sign vanishes. G identifies this sign as D mod 3 (resp. U mod 4; cf. the previous page). The condition is D ≡ 1 (3) (resp. U ≡ 1 (4)), automatic for A = Z_l with l ≠ 3 (resp. l ≠ 2).

Check: alpha = diag(-1,1) gives [alpha,rho] = [[-1,0],[2,-1]], with D = -1 ≢ 1 mod 3, as predicted.

Part II: G now studies the coupled equation (32) [alpha,rho] = [beta,sigma] eps_1(mu-1). The setting is general:
- G is a form of GL(2) attached to an Azumaya algebra M over S = Spec A.
- rho and sigma are regular sections (invertible sections of M).
- eps_1 : G_a -> SG is a one-parameter additive subgroup.

The case of interest (next page) is G = GL(2)_Z with eps_1(lambda) = [[1,0],[lambda,1]], so that eps_1(1) = rho sigma. He first plans to study the triples (xi, eta, mu) satisfying xi = eta eps_1(mu-1), det = 1 and the trace conditions.

This is the abelian/linear (SL2) shadow of the genus-1 / M_{1,1} part of the Galois action: mu plays the role of the cyclotomic character, and alpha, beta are the conjugating elements for the order-6 and order-4 generators.
errors: The trace condition for xi rho (as computed on the previous page) is C + D - B = 1. The transcribed (16) reads B + D - C = 1, which is a sign slip, either G's or the transcriber's. With alpha = diag(-1,1) one gets B + D - C = -3 but C + D - B = 1.

Point 1 is stated as a sufficient condition (D invertible), not as an equivalence. That is correct as stated. Over Z the regularity condition can only fail at p = 3 (resp. p = 2), so for Z_l with l ≠ 3 it is automatic once the trace and det conditions hold.
In point 3 the identification of the obstruction with D mod 3 is asserted without proof on this page. It is consistent with a direct check, but it presupposes D invertible mod 3.

ideas.what: Solvability of [alpha,rho] = xi in GL2(A) via conjugacy of the regular matrix xi rho to rho; obstruction to lifting to SL2 is det modulo norms of units of A[zeta_6] (resp. A[i]), detected by D mod 3 (resp. U mod 4)
ideas.modern_name: conjugacy classes of regular elements in GL2 over local rings / Latimer–MacDuffee; norm residue (Hilbert symbol) obstruction

ideas.what: Formulation of the loop equation [alpha,rho] = [beta,sigma] eps_1(mu-1) in a form G of GL2 attached to an Azumaya algebra, with regular sections rho, sigma and a one-parameter subgroup G_a -> SG
ideas.modern_name: SL2-image of the genus-one Grothendieck–Teichmüller relation (action on the profinite completion of SL2(Z) = pi_1 of M_{1,1})
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the Teichmüller tower and SL2 relations but not this computation

missed.claim: An explicit arithmetic criterion for the SL2/GL2 shadow of the loop equations. The commutator equations with the order-6 and order-4 generators of SL2(Z) are solvable in GL2(A) when D (resp. U) is a unit. Solvability in SL2 is governed by D mod 3 (resp. U mod 4), with only l = 3 (resp. l = 2) obstructed. This is elementary, but it is a concrete unpublished step in G's treatment of the genus-1 loop equations.
missed.quote: Pour qu'il y ait une solution dans Sl(2,A), il faut et suffit qu'on ait D ≡ 1 (3) (resp. U ≡ 1 (4))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows G working out the linear (SL2) reduction of the GT-type equations for M_{1,1} in the 1980s. This predates the published genus-one GT literature and is mildly relevant to the history of the subject; it is mathematically routine.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically elementary: conjugacy of regular 2x2 matrices plus a norm-residue sign. Historically it documents G's SL2/Azumaya-level analysis of the loop equation, which is consistent with known later work. Nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: '∫ (resp. y)' should read 'ξ (resp. η)'; likewise the marginal note reads 'Étude d'abord de l'équation en ξ, η'.
Struck word 'traff' is a cancelled start; the intended sense is 'le coefficient (terme) correspondant dans ρ^{-1} … et σ^{-1} … est zéro'.
The subscript of ε in (32) is overwritten (a 2 or 1 corrected to 1): ε_1(μ-1).
The struck heading 'I)' is corrected to 'II)'; the header insertion reads 'dans Gl(2)'.
